summary: Colfax County lookout above Cimarron, in use during a July 1963 fire; the FFLA lists it as gone. No build date or site description found.

facts.agency: State forestry (the 1963 clipping quotes the State Forester)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source we read describes what remains at the site or whether it can be reached.

events.note: A lookout at Turkey Tower reportedly saw a column of smoke from a fire in the Vernejo Park area
Vernejo Park area fire, reported in a July 2, 1963 clipping; a pilot estimated about 3,000 acres burned and a timber company manager said about 700 acres were destroyed

evidence.supports: Turkey Tower above Cimarron; lookout saw the fire; State Forester quoted
evidence.quote: The fire, in the Vernejo Park area, was seen by a lookout at Turkey Tower, above Cimarron, State Forester Ray Bell said.

evidence.supports: smoke column 20-25 miles northwest of the tower
evidence.quote: The lookout reportedly saw a huge column of smoke, 20-25 miles northwest of the tower.

evidence.supports: forestry pilot estimate of about 3,000 acres burned
evidence.quote: A Forestry Department pilot who scanned the area Sunday said about 3,000 acres were burned

evidence.supports: timber company manager estimate of about 700 acres destroyed
evidence.quote: Bud Lewis, manager of the Pacific Lumber Co., which has timber rights on the land, said about 700 acres were destroyed

evidence.supports: no fire protection agreement on the W.S. Gorley Ranch land
evidence.quote: The Forestry Department has no fire protection agreement on the land which is on the W.S. Gorley Ranch.

evidence.supports: clipping from the Hobbs Daily News-Sun
FFLA New Mexico list: Turkey, Colfax County, Tower, Gone

sources.title: Turkey - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (western US lookout history site)

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, one of them a 1963 newspaper clipping quoted on a lookout site. No build date, builder, design or fate date found, so the story leaves them out. Location problem for a human to check: the record point (36.24719, -105.65486) is roughly 70 km from Cimarron's centre (Wikipedia gives 36.50389, -104.89889), but the clipping places the tower above Cimarron and the smoke 20-25 miles northwest of it. No alternative coordinates were found, so no correction is proposed. The clipping gives two burned-area figures (about 3,000 acres from a Forestry Department pilot, about 700 acres destroyed per a timber company manager, Bud Lewis of Pacific Lumber Co.); the story reports both. The clipping's agency is State forestry; the record's State agency is consistent with it. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the clipping is dated July 2, 1963 and does not date the sighting, so the story no longer says early July.
